name: Nicholas Brady

summary.text: Nicholas F. Brady was U.S. Treasury Secretary from 1988 to 1993. On March 10, 1989, at a Brookings Institution and Bretton Woods Committee conference, he announced the initiative that became the Brady Plan, which departed from the Baker Plan by accepting that commercial-bank debt of heavily indebted countries would be reduced, with the IMF and World Bank supporting the exchange of bank loans for new bonds.

sources.title: US Third-World Debt Plan Praised. Treasury proposal includes debt forgiveness; IMF and World Bank would ease losses

facts.claim: On March 10, 1989 Treasury Secretary Brady announced a new initiative to deal with Latin America's debt problem in a speech at a Brookings Institution / Bretton Woods Committee conference.
facts.quote: on March 10 U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Nicholas Brady announced a new initiative to deal with Latin America's debt problem

sources.title: Plano Brady: da retórica à realidade

facts.claim: The Brady approach departed from the earlier Baker Plan, under which Treasury policy had held that all commercial-bank debt should eventually be repaid on market terms and which avoided debt forgiveness; the new plan accepted debt reduction supported by the IMF and World Bank.
facts.quote: eventually all of the commercial bank debt should be repaid on market terms

sources.title: Debt Relief by Private Creditors: Lessons from the Brady Plan

facts.claim: Under Brady Plan deals, debtor countries exchanged commercial-bank loans for new bonds covering principal and in some cases unpaid interest, with creditors choosing among options including discount bonds with reduced face value.
facts.quote: In exchange for commercial bank loans, the countries issued new bonds for the principal sum and, in some cases, unpaid interest.

sources.title: Debt Relief by Private Creditors: Lessons from the Brady Plan

facts.claim: Former Citicorp chairman Walter Wriston, whose view that countries do not go bankrupt had underpinned bank lending to developing countries, called the Brady plan 'a constructive contribution' in a 1989 interview while objecting to taxpayers bailing out banks.

sources.title: Flight of Capital Lies at Root of Latin America Debt Crisis

connections.claim: Brady was Secretary of the Treasury when he announced the Brady Plan in March 1989.
The Brady Plan relied on the IMF and World Bank to support debt-reduction deals between debtor countries and commercial banks.

openQuestions: The Treasury News transcript of Brady's March 10, 1989 speech was referenced but not opened; it should be cited as the primary source.
The exact Wriston phrasing 'countries don't go bankrupt' was not found verbatim in any source; Foreign Affairs paraphrases the view. No separate file was written for Walter Wriston.
